history.sg_progress: In the context of the Secretariat, and in particular regarding peacekeeping operations, the development of rules and mechanisms to identify acceptable risk- taking and experiment with ways to better incentivize and reward it remain extremely complex. Some mechanisms to incentivize and reward risk-taking within the existing framework do exist, such as the process for awarding bonuses (a risk premium), established by the General Assembly, to formed military and police units that have acquitted themselves well despite exceptional levels of risk and operate without restrictions and caveats. In the case of United Nations personnel, such a mechanism, if implemented, should cover all United Nations staff members, as the Staff Regulations and Rules describe the fundamental conditions of service and the basic rights, duties and obligations applicable to all staff in the Secretariat. A coordination meeting will be held with the Department of Peace Operations and the Department of Operational Support during the first half of 2024 in order to obtain a better perspective on implementing this recommendation.

history.recommendation_text: The Board also recommends that the Administration progressively develop mechanisms to define acceptable risk-taking at the level of peacekeeping missions and experiment with ways to better incentivize and reward it.
history.administration_response: The Administration stated that, in the context of the Secretariat and, in particular, peacekeeping operations, the development of rules and mechanisms to identify acceptable risk-taking and experiment with ways to better incentivize and reward it remained extremely complex. All heads of entities are responsible for the development and regular update of their entity-specific risk registers and for implementing their response plans. In this regard, all peacekeeping missions have identified, assessed and prioritized the most critical risks and have adopted an enterprise risk management process that includes the establishment of an appropriate governance structure, the assignment of risk management focal points and responsibilities and the operationalization of a dedicated risk management committee tasked with providing strategic guidance on the enterprise risk management implementation process. The Administration added that the old United Nations Competencies for the Future tool and the new Values and Behaviours Framework included risk- taking and that best practice would be disseminated.
history.board_assessment: The Board notes the Secretariat’s progress and will be attentive to the further dissemination of best practices on risk-taking.

history.sg_progress: The definition of acceptable risk-taking mechanisms is closely tied to the concept of risk tolerance. However, the development of clear and objective rules and mechanisms for acceptable risk-taking remains a complex endeavour in the context of the Secretariat and requires a culture change. To address the issue, the Office of Human Resources rolled out various managerial tools and frameworks encouraging risk-taking by looking for new and improved ways to deliver on programmes. For example, in the old United Nations Competencies for the Future tool, risk-taking was emphasized in both the managerial and core competencies. Under the “vision” competency, identifying strategic issues, opportunities and risks was one of the behavioural indicators that demonstrated the competency in practice. Similarly, under the “managing performance” competency, one of the behavioural indicators was to encourage risk-taking and support creativity and initiative. Furthermore, under the new United Nations Values and Behaviours Framework, the Office of Human Resources encourages reasoned decision-making, including risk-taking. For example, under the “analyse and plan” behaviour, senior leaders are expected to detect and interpret early signals, new and emerging trends, opportunities and risks. Similarly, under the “deliver results with positive impact” behaviour, senior leaders are expected to take calculated risks, as necessary. The Administration considers this recommendation to have been implemented and requests its closure by the Board.

history.recommendation_text: The Board also recommends that the Administration progressively develop mechanisms to define acceptable risk-taking at the level of peacekeeping missions and experiment with ways to better incentivize and reward it.
history.administration_response: The concept of acceptable risk-taking is linked intrinsically to the broader notion of risk tolerance. However, developing clear and objective mechanisms for acceptable risk-taking within the context of the United Nations Secretariat remains a complex undertaking, requiring not only structural changes, but also a broader cultural shift. To help to foster this change, the Office of Human Resources promotes responsible risk-taking through a variety of managerial tools and frameworks that support innovation and more effective programme delivery. To further promote knowledge-sharing, the Department of Management Strategy, Policy and Compliance will disseminate best practices from field missions through a dedicated community of practice, highlighting the positive impacts of enterprise risk management implementation, sharing success stories and capturing lessons learned.
history.board_assessment: The Board notes the existing tools and frameworks. The dissemination of good practice, which is a key element, was already mentioned. The Board will be attentive to the deployment of a dedicated community of practice. In the meantime, the recommendation is considered under implementation.
